title: Technician eligibility and dispatch
body: Skills and certification gate eligibility
Local hours, time off and existing bookings constrain appointments
Recommendations reserve no capacity
notes: Dispatch starts with eligibility before it considers a score. The Scheduling service retrieves the authorized order, technician profiles and time-off records, then combines them with its own confirmed bookings. Skill, certification, availability and local working hours decide whether a candidate can perform this appointment. The baseline ranks feasible technicians by existing workload. An explanation lets the dispatcher review those contributing facts. Confirming the booking repeats the checks and lets PostgreSQL reject a concurrent overlap. The screenshot shows the real dispatch screen. Next, follow the technician's ordered service procedure. Source: SchedulingRecommendations.cs and booking constraint migration 002.

title: Eight-stage guided service
body: Eight ordered stages use immutable template v1
Visible dropdown choices receive server validation
Completed stages remain read-only history
Assistance handles exceptions honestly
notes: The procedure moves from acceptance through arrival, inspection, diagnosis, repair, quality verification and customer confirmation to completion. Each workflow pins a template version rather than silently adopting a changed form. The backend validates the current stage and its visible allowed answers. A conditional delay reason appears only when travel is delayed, and hidden answers cannot bypass validation. Completed stages preserve their recorded answers as history. When none of the choices fits, the technician can request assistance instead of inventing a response. TemplateTests covers version and option rules. The next slide explains the server clock behind the countdown.

title: Durable stage SLA
body: 20 minutes: technician warning
25 minutes: critical technician warning
30 minutes: supervisor escalation
Persisted UTC deadlines recover after restart
notes: The service persists a stage's UTC start and deadline when that stage activates. Quartz evaluates durable state, so a process restart does not reset the clock. A sweep can catch up missing warning, critical and breach milestones after downtime. The twenty-five-minute critical warning still targets the technician. The thirty-minute breach adds the supervisor escalation. Approved pauses extend effective duration while preserving any earlier breach. A late submission evaluates outstanding thresholds before completing its stage. The local resilience script verified restart and breach behavior using explicitly labeled seconds. Next, compare the two dispatch strategies and their measured tradeoffs.

title: Intelligent scheduling tradeoffs
body: Operational advice uses actual scoped availability
CP-SAT enforces hard appointment constraints
Synthetic benchmark: 22 jobs assigned by both strategies
647 versus 619 proxy travel minutes; FEASIBLE
notes: The operational adapter evaluates one fixed appointment with real authorized staff, working hours, time off and bookings. It calls OR-Tools and independently checks the returned assignment. Operational travel remains null because the system has no recorded geocoded routes. A separate six-technician, twenty-two-job synthetic comparison measures the batch solver. Both strategies assigned every job. The depot travel proxy was six hundred forty-seven minutes for baseline and six hundred nineteen for optimized, while workload spread increased slightly and runtime increased. The solver returned FEASIBLE, not proven optimal. These are measured tradeoffs on one dataset. Next, observe how operational signals reach people.

title: Alerts and supervisor intervention
body: Events create deduplicated persisted notifications
Signed identities select team or technician groups
SignalR supplements authoritative history
Acknowledgments and interventions retain evidence
notes: Notifications turn workflow events into task-focused alerts. A unique source event identity prevents duplicate messages from becoming duplicate business notifications. The consumer commits history before sending its best-effort SignalR update. The hub places a signed technician or team identity into its authorized group. A disconnected client can recover from persisted history, which remains the source of truth. The live WebSocket check matched a received supervisor notice to its stored notification ID and denied analyst and anonymous hub access. Acknowledgments and reasoned supervisor actions produce further evidence. Next, inspect the incident rather than relying on a screenshot of its latest state.

title: Operational Replay and investigation
body: Original business events remain immutable
Delivery attempts and terminal faults stay separate
Playback reconstructs historical state
Facts, uncertainty and trace retention stay explicit
notes: Replay assembles one work order's retained evidence without querying every operational database. It preserves the original envelope and hash, then stores delivery observations separately. Causation and source-local sequences help order events, while missing parents and independent ordering remain visible as uncertainty. Playback moves a historical cursor and reconstructs read state. It never resubmits a form or booking command. The controlled incident includes a failed warning delivery, retry, breach, supervisor intervention and completion. Its factual summary does not infer a root cause. Trace links require a scoped retention check. Next, consider advice that may help before a future deadline is missed.

title: Predictive SLA advice
body: Synthetic chronological split: 60% train, 20% calibrate, 20% test
Logistic F1 0.754; rule F1 0.442
False-alert rate 0.242 versus 0.170
Supervisors retain decision authority
notes: The model predicts whether an active stage will exceed its SLA from information available at the snapshot. One observation per stage and chronological training, calibration and test partitions reduce leakage. The measured synthetic logistic model achieved F1 of zero point seven five four versus zero point four four two for the rule baseline. Its false-alert rate was higher, so detection improved at a cost. The interface exposes assumptions, factors, model version and prediction time. Supervisors record accepted or dismissed advice with a reason. No real-world accuracy or employee ranking claim follows from this synthetic evaluation. Next, separate implemented experiments from the simulator roadmap.

title: Digital Operations Simulator roadmap
body: Implemented: deterministic tests and bounded resilience scenarios
Implemented: synthetic model and dispatch evaluation
Planned: interactive absence, surge and what-if simulation
notes: A broad Digital Operations Simulator is planned rather than implemented. The repository already contains useful narrower experiments: deterministic clock-driven tests, synthetic model and solver evaluation, accelerated SLA transitions, broker outage and controlled consumer failures. They provide reproducible evidence for selected mechanisms. They do not form an interactive business simulation of arbitrary absences or demand surges. A future simulator would need explicit assumptions, repeatable scenario inputs and independently validated outcomes. Keeping that boundary visible prevents a roadmap label from becoming a false completion claim. The next slide returns to a capability already implemented in the native client's queue.

title: Native offline synchronization
body: Owner-scoped cache, drafts and durable operation queue
Original key, version and client time survive retries
Backoff and manual synchronization preserve conflicts
Server access and SLA remain authoritative
notes: Disconnection preserves useful local work without creating a second workflow authority. The device persists each logical action with its owner, original idempotency key, expected version, answers and client-reported time. Automatic retries back off. Manual synchronization may retry timing-eligible work immediately, but it cannot force a blocked conflict through. Server version and access checks still decide acceptance, and offline time does not pause an SLA. Tokens use SecureStore, while drafts and caches use account-scoped AsyncStorage without application encryption. Source tests cover these rules. The native demonstration must separately establish which device transitions actually occurred. Next, move into the running web application.

title: Native Android architecture

SecureStore protects credentials

title: Business evidence and technical observability

OpenTelemetry follows technical execution
Prometheus and Grafana expose service health
Trace retention can expire independently
notes: Replay and observability answer related but different questions. A business event records an accepted transition and its actor, while traces expose technical execution across requests and messaging. Prometheus scrapes service metrics, Grafana displays them, and structured logs retain correlation context. The latest retained observability artifact records six healthy targets and a business trace with twenty-seven spans. Those counts describe that observation, not an availability guarantee. Jaeger uses bounded in-memory retention, so a trace may disappear while immutable business evidence survives. The application checks availability before offering its link. title: Security controls and release gaps
body: Signed identity plus role and resource policies
Owner migrations and restricted runtime grants
Redacted analytics and no committed credentials
TLS, restore drills and full audits remain deployment work
notes: Security starts with signed identity and continues at each object boundary. Backend role policies and team or technician checks remain necessary even when navigation hides a page. Migration credentials are separate from runtime identities, and replay evidence permits ordinary insertion without mutation. Warehouse staging removes customer contact details and answers. Local secret, static and dependency scans provide scoped evidence, while the passive pre-login ZAP result is not an authenticated ASVS assessment. Production TLS, identity policy, secret rotation and tested backup restoration still require a hosting target. Accessibility checks also have a stated scope. Next, examine the implementation challenges that made these boundaries necessary.

title: Engineering challenges
body: Reliable deadlines across restart and late submission
Meaningful ordering across independent services
Native OAuth, account isolation and offline conflicts
Windows toolchain and migration/runtime separation
notes: The difficult work centered on state and evidence rather than adding screens. Durable deadlines needed restart catch-up without emitting duplicate milestones. Replay needed causal and source-local order without pretending device timestamps created a reliable global sequence. Native authentication had to coordinate browser return, credential persistence and refreshes that outlived logout. Offline actions needed explicit conflict handling instead of silently changing the expected version. Operationally, Windows path handling required an updated local Ninja tool, and database grants required a separate owner migration path. These are observed engineering problems with concrete fixes and remaining limits. Next, consider the broader architectural tradeoffs behind them.

title: Architecture tradeoffs
body: Service isolation adds deployment and consistency cost
Synchronous checks and asynchronous projections serve different needs
Offline continuity creates explicit conflict work
Bounded optimization trades runtime for feasible advice
notes: Microservices provide clear ownership and independent deployment units, but they require more configuration and leave cross-service races to be managed explicitly. A modular monolith would be a reasonable alternative for a smaller team. Synchronous checks help validate a booking now, while asynchronous events let reporting and alerts recover independently at the cost of lag. Offline continuity preserves work but exposes version conflicts that a connected-only client might avoid. Bounded CP-SAT can return feasible advice without proving optimality, and the measured runtime is higher than greedy ranking. These choices are contextual rather than universally superior. Next, prioritize improvements using the remaining evidence gaps.

title: Prioritized roadmap
body: Complete native recovery and physical-device acceptance
Validate target-specific security, retention and restore
Resolve cross-service race and capacity edge cases
Measure realistic load and operational routing before scale claims
notes: The roadmap follows operational impact. First, close any native submission, reconnect and conflict steps not established by the final recording, then test physical devices and release packaging. A real deployment needs TLS, managed secrets, identity policy and a restore drill before handling customer data. Cross-service cancellation and profile races deserve explicit coordination, and capacity calculations need further interval-edge validation. Only then should realistic load tests and geocoded routing support scalability or travel claims. The SCD2 source already exists, but retained history limits still matter. Template authoring and a general simulator remain later product work. Next, summarize the engineering outcomes supported today.

Conflict-protected booking and ordered service execution
Immutable investigation, warehouse reporting and advisory intelligence
Local tests and controlled recovery provide inspectable evidence
notes: The result is an inspectable local engineering system with six service owners and shared authenticated client capabilities. PostgreSQL protects confirmed appointment overlap, while the workflow service governs ordered forms and durable deadlines. Immutable replay connects business transitions with delivery observations, warehouse projections and technical traces. Advisory prediction and optimization expose assumptions and measured synthetic results. Local tests and controlled failures make these mechanisms reviewable. They do not establish production adoption, uptime, savings or certified mobile release quality. The delivered evidence inventory keeps those boundaries attached to the claims.
